headline: Approves up to $30,000 for Instruction Partners to coach teacher leaders in math at EnCompass Academy
summary: Instruction Partners, based in Nashville, will build the skills of instructional teacher leaders at EnCompass Academy so that high-poverty students, multilingual learners, foster or homeless youth, and students with disabilities have access to high-quality instruction. It will provide coaching, school walkthroughs and teacher learning sessions focused on math. The agreement runs August 8, 2023 through June 30, 2024. The service period began before this vote.
outcome_action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

title: Services Agreement 2023-2024 - Thena Gee Consulting - Early Childhood Development Department
official_text: Ratification by the Board of Education of a Services Agreement 2023-2024 by and between the District and Thena Gee Consulting, Sunnyvale, CA, for the latter to provide virtual Effective Mindfulness, Building Responsive and Confident Educators (EMBRACE) training and coaching to reinforce concepts and strategies to support the transfer of practices; introduce core practices to create strength-based environments that support educators and children’s health and resiliency; to positively influence the culture and climate in early childhood settings and ultimately improve child outcomes, via Early Childhood Development Department, for the period of March 4, 2024 through June 30, 2024, in an amount not to exceed $4,200.00.
headline: Approves up to $4,200 for Thena Gee Consulting to train early childhood educators in mindfulness
summary: Thena Gee Consulting, based in Sunnyvale, will provide virtual training and coaching called Effective Mindfulness, Building Responsive and Confident Educators (EMBRACE). It aims to create strength-based environments that support educators and children's health and resilience in early childhood settings. The agreement is through the Early Childhood Development Department and runs March 4, 2024 through June 30, 2024. The Board is ratifying it after the service period began.
outcome_action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

title: Measures N and H – College and Career Readiness Commission - Oakland High School - 2022-2023 Education Improvement Plan/ Budget Modification
official_text: Adoption by the Board of Education, upon recommendation of the Measures N and H Commission, of a 2022-2023 Education Improvement Plan/Budget modification for Oakland High School reducing $7,000 by $269.50 to $6,730.50 for Teacher Salary Stipends: Extended Contracts to pay the Teachers from the (Tigers) 9th Grade Family for Professional Learning Community Services and establishing a new expenditure in the amount of $269.50 for Professional Contracted Services: Funds to pay for transportation costs on the San Francisco Ferry and a field trip to the Exploratorium and Aquarium of the Bay, as stated in the justification section of the New or Revised Strategic Action Section of the Budget Modification Form.
presenter: Measures N and H - College and Career Readiness Commission
headline: Moves $269.50 within Oakland High's budget to pay for ferry and field trip transportation
summary: On the recommendation of the Measures N and H Commission, the board is asked to change Oakland High School's 2022-2023 plan. A teacher stipend line for 9th grade family teachers' professional learning community work is cut by $269.50, from $7,000 to $6,730.50. A new $269.50 line pays transportation costs for the San Francisco Ferry and a field trip to the Exploratorium and Aquarium of the Bay. No new money is added.
outcome_action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

group: Measures N and H Commission - Chairperson David Kakishiba - March 5, 2024
title: Measures N and H – College and Career Readiness Commission - High School Linked Learning Office - 2022-2023 Education Improvement Plan/ Budget Modification
official_text: Adoption by the Board of Education, upon recommendation of the Measures N and H Commission, of 2022-2023 Education Improvement Plan/Budget modification for the High School Linked Learning Office reducing the Admin 10% budget of $7,000 for Professional Contracted Services by $7000; reducing the Admin 10% budget of $2,000 for Supplies and Materials by $2,000; reducing the Admin 10% budget of $11,000 for Professional Contracted Services by $11,000 and to transfer the total amount of $20,000 creating a new expenditure of $20,000 for Professional contracted services with Amy Crudo, as stated in the justification section of the New or Revised Strategic Action Section of the Budget Modification Form.
presenter: Measures N and H - College and Career Readiness Commission
headline: Shifts $20,000 of Linked Learning Office administrative funds to a consultant contract
summary: On the recommendation of the Measures N and H Commission, the board is asked to change the High School Linked Learning Office's 2022-2023 plan. Three administrative budget lines (two for professional contracted services and one for supplies and materials) are cut by $7,000, $2,000 and $11,000. Together, $20,000 is moved to a new line for professional contracted services with Amy Crudo. No new money is added.
outcome_action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

group: Measures N and H Commission - Chairperson David Kakishiba - March 5, 2024
title: Measures N and H – College and Career Readiness Commission - High School Linked Learning Office - 2022-2023 Education Improvement Plan/ Budget Modification
official_text: Adoption by the Board of Education, upon recommendation of the Measures N and H Commission, of a 2022-2023 Education Improvement Plan/Budget modification for the High School Linked Learning Office to reduce $45,150 Teacher Salaries Stipends: Extended Contracts for 43 Pathway Leads to participate in the Linked Learning Leadership Institute by $25,000 to $20,150 and modifying an existing expenditure of $50,000 by $25,000 for Consultant Contract with Connect Ed to support Linked Learning Coach training totaling $75,000, as stated in the justification section of the New or Revised Strategic Action Section of the Budget Modification Form.
presenter: Measures N and H - College and Career Readiness Commission
headline: Shifts $25,000 within the Linked Learning Office budget to raise a Connect Ed coaching contract to $75,000
summary: On the recommendation of the Measures N and H Commission, the board is asked to change the High School Linked Learning Office's 2022-2023 plan. A stipend line for 43 Pathway Leads to attend the Linked Learning Leadership Institute is cut by $25,000, from $45,150 to $20,150. That $25,000 raises an existing consultant contract with Connect Ed, which supports Linked Learning Coach training, from $50,000 to $75,000. No new money is added.
outcome_action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

title: Change Order No. 1, Agreement Between Owner and Contractor – Mar Con Builders, Inc. – Kaiser Child Development Center Site Improvements Project – Division of Facilities Planning and Management
official_text:
Approval by the Board of Education of Change Order No. 1, Agreement Between Owner and Contractor by and between the District and Mar Con Builders, Inc., Oakland, CA, for the latter to perform: 
·	PCO #12 for installation of 3 new play structures.
·	PCO #13 for 6" wide 24" deep concrete curb placed as a divider between pavers and existing asphalt.
·	PCO #14 for expansion joints needed at retaining wall.
·	PCO #15 for demolition of concrete apron that is not ADA compliant
for the Kaiser Child Development Center Site Improvements Project, in the additional amount of $156,911.00, increasing the not to exceed amount of the Agreement from $6,551,440.00 to $6,708,351.00; and extending the term of the Agreement by an additional 239 Calendar Days, from June 8, 2023 through November 4, 2023 to June 30, 2024. All other terms and conditions of the Agreement remain in full force and effect.
presenter: Deputy Chief, Facilities Planning and Management
headline: Adds $156,911 and 239 days to Mar Con Builders' Kaiser Child Development Center site project
summary: This change order adds $156,911 to the contract with Mar Con Builders, raising the not-to-exceed amount from $6,551,440 to $6,708,351. The added work is three new play structures, a concrete curb between pavers and existing asphalt, expansion joints at a retaining wall, and demolition of a concrete apron that does not meet Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) accessibility rules. It also extends the contract by 239 calendar days, from November 4, 2023 to June 30, 2024.
outcome_action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

title: Amendment No. 1, General Services Agreement – Sandis Civil Engineers Surveyors Planners – East Oakland Pride Site Improvements Project - Division of Facilities Planning and Management
official_text: Approval by the Board of Education of Amendment No. 1, General Services Agreement by and between the District and Sandis Civil Engineers Surveyors Planners, Pleasanton, CA., for the latter to provide additional underground potholing work deemed necessary to identify the nature of the unknown utilities on site, as described in the Proposal dated, February 21, 2024, attached to this Amendment as Exhibit A, for the East Oakland Pride Site Improvements Project, in the additional amount of $12,100.00, increasing the Agreement’s not to exceed cost from $37,950.00 to $50,050.00, with an unchanged term date of July 1, 2023 through June 30, 2024. All other terms and conditions of the Agreement remain in full force and effect.
presenter: Deputy Chief, Facilities Planning and Management
headline: Adds $12,100 for Sandis to probe for unknown underground utilities at the East Oakland Pride site
summary: This amendment adds $12,100 to the agreement with Sandis Civil Engineers Surveyors Planners, raising the not-to-exceed cost from $37,950 to $50,050. The added work is underground potholing (digging small test holes) to identify unknown utilities at the East Oakland Pride Site Improvements Project. The term is unchanged: July 1, 2023 through June 30, 2024.
outcome_action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

title: Change Order No. 1, Agreement Between Owner and Contractor - Deco Tech Systems - Castlemont High School Security Improvement Project - Division of Facilities Planning and Management
official_text: Approval by the Board of Education of Change Order No. 1, Agreement Between Owner and Contractor, by and between the District and Deco Tech Systems, Walnut Creek, CA, for additional software services deemed necessary to improve the user experience, software experience, and a server upgrade, more specifically described in PCO 1, incorporated herein by reference as though fully set forth, for the Castlemont High School Security Improvement Project, in the additional amount of $8,375.50, increasing the not to exceed amount of the Agreement from $323,000.00 to $331,387.50. All other terms and conditions of the Agreement remain in full force and effect.
presenter: Deputy Chief, Facilities Planning and Management
headline: Adds $8,375.50 for Deco Tech Systems' security software upgrades at Castlemont High School
summary: This change order adds $8,375.50 to the contract with Deco Tech Systems for the Castlemont High School Security Improvement Project. The added work is software services to improve the user experience and a server upgrade. The text says the not-to-exceed amount rises from $323,000 to $331,387.50, which is $12 more than the old total plus the added amount.
outcome_action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

title: Agreement Between Owner and Contractor – DecoTech Systems, Inc. - Cole Data Center Relocation Project – Division of Facilities Planning and Management
official_text: Approval by the Board of Education of an Agreement Between Owner and Contractor by and between the District and DecoTech Systems, Inc., Walnut Creek, CA, for the latter to relocate the data center equipment and reinstall the services from the existing building to the new building for the Cole Data Center Relocation Project, in the not-to-exceed amount of $147,400.00 which includes a not-to-exceed general contingency allowance amount of $13,400.00 with the work scheduled to commence on April 11, 2024, and scheduled to last until April 30, 2025.
presenter: Deputy Chief, Facilities Planning and Management
headline: Pays DecoTech Systems up to $147,400 to move the Cole data center equipment to a new building
summary: DecoTech Systems, Inc. will relocate the data center equipment and reinstall services from the existing building to the new building for the Cole Data Center Relocation Project. The not-to-exceed amount is $147,400, which includes a $13,400 general contingency allowance. Work is scheduled to start April 11, 2024 and last until April 30, 2025.
outcome_action: Adopted on the General Consent Report
